skill.name: agent-tools

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily operational documentation for a hosted AI CLI, and most findings are safe documentation patterns. The installer pipes a remote script to a shell, reads API credentials, and uses remote manifest data in command substitution, so those findings remain confirmed; social-media posting also creates a separate business-logic risk.

remediation.issue: The installation instructions pipe a remote script directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Publish a versioned installer or package, download it first, verify a pinned checksum or signature, and then run it.

remediation.issue: The manual installation example uses command substitution to select a download URL from a remote manifest.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the release URL and verify its signature or checksum before extraction. Avoid parsing untrusted remote metadata in a shell command.

remediation.issue: The documentation instructs users to provide API keys through an environment variable.
remediation.suggestion: Document secret-manager and CI masking practices, prevent accidental logging, and explain how to rotate and revoke exposed keys.

remediation.issue: The skill documents posting and other social-media actions through hosted apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, narrow permissions, preview content, and apply rate limits before any post, message, follow, like, or retweet.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with the inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: Running many hosted AI models often requires separate commands and input formats. This skill organizes discovery, authentication, file uploads, task tracking, and app execution through one CLI workflow.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install, authenticate, update, and check the inference.sh CLI.
Shows how to browse, search, filter, and inspect hosted applications.
Provides command patterns for image, video, text, search, audio, and 3D applications.
Explains how to pass inline inputs, input files, local media, and version-pinned apps.
Shows how to submit asynchronous tasks and retrieve their status or results.
limitations: It does not run models itself or provide GPU capacity.
Available apps, models, pricing, quotas, and input schemas depend on the hosted platform.
Commands require a separately installed CLI and valid account authentication.
The documentation does not guarantee output quality, safety, or availability from third-party apps.

use_cases.title: Prototype media workflows
use_cases.description: Find image, video, audio, or 3D apps and run them with structured inputs.

use_cases.title: Connect hosted models to projects
use_cases.description: Use CLI commands, input files, and task tracking to test hosted models in development workflows.

use_cases.title: Automate research tasks
use_cases.description: Run hosted language models and search apps for repeatable research and content workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run a first app
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to authenticate the inference.sh CLI and run one image-generation app with a simple prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Discover the right app
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search the app store for a hosted video model, inspect its input schema, and choose a suitable app.

prompt_templates.title: Process a local file
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a command workflow that sends a local image to an upscaling app, saves the result, and checks the task status.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reliable pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a version-pinned inference.sh workflow for a production prototype with input validation, asynchronous tasks, retries, secret handling, and output tracking.

output_examples.input: I need to turn a local product image into a short video.
output_examples.output: A workflow that selects an image-to-video app, passes the local image path, submits the job, and checks the task result.

output_examples.input: How can I find a hosted model for technical research?
output_examples.output: A discovery workflow that searches the app store, filters by category, inspects app details, and compares input requirements.

output_examples.input: I need a repeatable image generation test.
output: Create a sample input and edit the prompt.
Run the task and record the returned result.

best_practices: Inspect an app schema and generate a sample input before running it.
Pin app versions for repeatable tests and review hosted-app permissions.
Keep API keys in a protected secret manager and confirm external side effects.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe an unreviewed remote installer directly into a shell.
Do not upload sensitive local files to hosted apps without approval.
Do not automate social-media actions without previews, limits, and confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It explains inference.sh CLI workflows. The hosted platform performs the actual model execution.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a valid inference.sh account and authentication before running hosted apps.

faq.question: Can I use local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented CLI workflow accepts local paths for fields that support file or URL inputs.

faq.question: Can I run long jobs asynchronously?
faq.answer: Yes. Submit a job without waiting, then use its task identifier to check status and retrieve results.

faq.question: Does it support Claude?
faq.answer: The documentation includes Claude through a hosted OpenRouter application, subject to current platform availability.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production automation?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance, but production use requires secret management, version pinning, validation, limits, and failure handling.
